Key.Original: Manufacturer: Gustloff-Werke%1Length: 34.8 inches%1Ammunition: 7.92×33mm Kurz%1Rate of Fire: 600 rpm%1Weight: 4.6kg%1Firing Mode(s): Semi-Automatic%1Magazine: 30-round detachable box magazine%1Effective Range: 300 meters%1%1The MP 507, also known as the Gustloff Volkssturmgewehr, is a semi-automatic rifle that saw service during the closing months of the Second World War. Chambered in 7.92×33mm Kurz, the MP 507 used the same detachable 30-round box magazine as the StG 44. Designed for the Primitiv-Waffen-Programm, it had a simple gas-delayed blowback action based on the Barnitzke system.
